transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start time: 14:23 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Diaz (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Jun Li (Solutions Eng) — Redwood; Liam O'Connor (Head of ML); Priya Rao (Platform Eng); Jordan Smith (Security); Asha Menon (Data Eng) — NexaHealth

Summary (auto): quick POC check-in: validated initial benchmark results, identified tuning steps for batching/quantization, environment access blockers (VPC/roles), SSO and KMS questions; agreed next steps and deadlines.

Topics: onboarding progress; access setup (VPC, IAM); env readiness for dedicated inference tests; security/compliance checklist; tuning results (latency/cost tradeoffs); next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 40 minutes today, quick check-in on the pilot — how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Liam (NexaHealth): good thanks, yeah excited to see the next set of numbers. we've been trying to reproduce dev runs, a few snags on our side with the VPC peering.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood): quick note — we pushed the latest benchmark with the prefix caching enabled, also a version that uses 4-bit quantization for the model variant.
[00:24] Priya (NexaHealth): yeah we saw the file but we don't yet have the test account connected, still waiting on the cross-account IAM roles from infra.
[00:30] Carlos: ok great, so agenda — review results, confirm what tuning we did, list the access steps, and security questions. also — call out any blockers for the Dedicated run.
[00:41] Jun (Redwood): i'll walk through the numbers. the baseline run (hosted) was about 220ms p50 for short prompts, p95 ~480ms, token cost estimated at $0.002/token in our sheet. the dedicated run with batching dropped cost by ~30% but p95 went up a bit to ~530ms.
[01:05] Liam: can you clarify "batching" — is that continuous batching on the runtime or explicit queueing? we have latency SLOs under 600ms for our interactive UI.
[01:12] Maya: good question — it's continuous batching in the runtime; Redwood does dynamic batch formation with a max-latency cap, we tuned cap to 60ms during the test which trades throughput for tail latency.
[01:26] Priya: the p95 at 530ms is acceptable, but we need steady-state testing over 24h with our seq-length distribution, do you have examples of seq-length histos?
[01:36] Jun: yes we included a small histogram in the sheet (tab: distributions). note the hosted test used shorter seqs by mistake — will re-run with your distribution.
[01:45] Carlos: action item — Carlos to re-run with NexaHealth seq distribution and send updated CSV.
[01:51] Liam: also curious about KV cache behavior — we saw cache hits drop after user turnover, how is prefix caching handled in Dedicated?
[01:58] Maya: KV cache is sticky per worker shard, we support prefix-level caching and optional sticky routing. in Dedicated it's possible to set cache affinity to keep hot keys on the same pool. there was a small transcribe error in the sheet that said "KV-cache is stateless" — that is wrong, thanks for catching.
[02:18] Jordan (Security): quick security question — we need to confirm KMS integration and whether Redwood can use our CMKs; plus audit log retention.
[02:27] Carlos: yes for Private/Dedicated we support bring-your-own-CMK via AWS KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs can be exported to your S3/CloudWatch with configurable retention.
[02:36] Jordan: do you have docs on encryption at rest & in transit? we need SOC2 artefacts.
[02:41] Maya: i've got the SOC2 summary and encryption page — i'll share links after the call.
[02:46] Asha (Data Eng): on access setup — we tried the handshake but the peering request timed out, probably a CIDR overlap.
[02:54] Priya: yep, our infra flagged overlapping cidr 10.0.0.0/16 with another team.
[03:00] Carlos: ok, so next step — Priya to confirm a non-conflicting CIDR and provide the CIDR and IAM role ARNs, we'll use that to provision the dev VPC access.
[03:10] Jun: on benchmarking details — we ran both a quantized variant (4-bit) and fp16; quantization reduced memory footprint by ~40% and allowed denser packing on the GPU which improved cost but added some hallucination risk on long context.
[03:25] Liam: hallucination risk is a concern for us for clinical prompts, do you have quality regression numbers?
[03:31] Maya: we included a small eval set — accuracy delta was within our threshold for short prompts but for longer, some degradation. recommendation: use fp16 for critical flows and q4 for lower-risk background tasks.
[03:45] Priya: can we run A/B with traffic split in the Dedicated pilot? we'd like to test q4 vs fp16 in parallel.
[03:52] Carlos: yes, rollouts are supported — we can do canary and automatic fallback if quality drops below your thresholds. we'll need the eval prompts and failure criteria.
[04:04] Liam: we'll send a list of ~200 eval prompts by end of week.
[04:09] Jun: note about routing — smart routing can send high-priority requests to lower-latency pool, and cheaper requests to a quantized pool. that helps keep UI SLOs while saving cost.
[04:20] Jordan: on compliance — we need RBAC and audit trails for who called which model and what the prompt was; how granular are your logs?
[04:28] Maya: we log route, model version, token counts, and hashed prompts by default; full prompt logging can be enabled but we recommend hashed or redacted prompts for PHI.
[04:38] Jordan: okay, we'll discuss retention policy — we need 7 years for some study, might be heavy; can you export to our S3?
[04:45] Carlos: yes export is supported, retention policy is configurable; we'll include that in the security doc.
[04:52] Priya: another blocker — our CI doesn't yet have the terraform module for the Redwood Private control plane. is there a published module?
[04:59] Maya: we have a community terraform module and an enterprise module — i'll share the enterprise terraform snippet for VPC + roles, it's not long.
[05:07] Asha: please ensure the module includes endpoints for the metrics exporter, we need prometheus hooks.
[05:12] Jun: exporter is optional, but yes we expose Prometheus endpoints and can push metrics to your prometheus via a relay.
[05:19] Liam: circling back to numbers — can you also include cost-per-1000-tokens for both hosted and dedicated in the new benchmark? that helps our finance.
[05:27] Carlos: will do, cost per 1k tokens for each config and a projected monthly cost at your expected QPS.
[05:33] Priya: timeline — we want the Dedicated smoke test next week if access is ready.
[05:38] Carlos: target: smoke test on 2027-08-18, assuming we get VPC + roles by 2027-08-12 and bench re-run by 2027-08-13.
[05:46] Jordan: one more — SSO. we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning, can Redwood support auto-provisioning?
[05:55] Maya: yes SCIM + SAML supported; for Private we can do IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. we'll send a checklist for the SSO setup.
[06:03] Liam: any known gotchas with cross-region Dedicated runs? we might route some traffic to eu-west for latency reasons.
[06:12] Jun: model variants must be compatible across regions; there can be slight perf differences due to hardware generation, but fallbacks are automatic if a region is saturated.
[06:21] Priya: oh and what about model pinning — we need ability to pin to a specific model/artifact during the pilot.
[06:27] Carlos: yes pinning is supported per route, and we can do canary rollouts.
[06:33] Asha: do you support drift detection for model outputs? we want alerts on quality regressions.
[06:38] Maya: Redwood Optimize has regression alerts tied to eval sets; we'll configure it for your eval suite.
[06:44] Liam: ok great.
[06:46] (brief crosstalk)
[07:05] Carlos: quick recap — owners and dates: Carlos send updated bench + cost (8/13), Priya provide CIDR and IAM ARNs (8/12), Maya send SSO and SOC2 docs (8/14), Jordan send encryption/retention reqs (8/16). smoke test planned 8/18.
[07:27] Liam: sounds good. thanks.
[07:31] Carlos: any blockers we missed?
[07:34] Priya: none from infra once CIDR is confirmed.
[07:37] Jordan: none from security aside from docs.
[07:40] Carlos: ok we'll follow up via email with the sheet and links. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Call recap (auto):
- Benchmarks: hosted vs dedicated numbers reviewed; re-run with customer seq-length distribution.
- Tuning: q4 reduces cost but some quality delta; recommend fp16 for critical flows.
- Access: VPC peering/CIDR + IAM ARNs required to provision dev account for smoke test.
- Security: KMS BYO-CMK supported; SOC2 + SAML/SCIM docs to be shared.
- Next major milestone: Dedicated smoke test on 2027-08-18.

Referenced artifacts/links (to be shared): benchmark_sheet.csv, SOC2_summary.pdf, SSO_SCIM_checklist.md, terraform-enterprise-snippet.tf

- Carlos Diaz: share re-run results + cost estimates (due 2027-08-13)
- Priya Rao: confirm non-overlapping CIDR and provide IAM ARNs (due 2027-08-12)
- Maya Patel: share SSO/SAML + SOC2 docs and terraform snippet (due 2027-08-14)
